# Ovaar

> Software engineering notes by Thomas Reynders on C++ and Conan, Python tooling, CI pipelines, 3D on the web and working with coding agents. Written by Thomas Reynders, a software engineer in Leeuwarden (NL).

All writing is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. Full post text is also in the RSS feed: https://ovaar.github.io/index.xml

## About

- [About Thomas Reynders](https://ovaar.github.io/about/): background, current work and links

## Posts

- [A lint ratchet: from 97 useEffects to 2 in a week](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/lint-ratchet-useeffect/): How a custom lint rule plus a shrink-only exceptions list took a React codebase from 97 effects in components to 2, and why most of them were deleted rather than moved.
- [A robot that clicks around staging every night](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/nightly-seeded-random-walk-e2e/): A seeded random walk in Playwright that checks every screen for crashes, server errors and leaked translation keys, cannot write tenant data, and found a WebGL viewer leak on its second night.
- [C# performance 2: cutting allocations, then and now](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/csharp-performance-allocations/): My 2020 list of C# allocation tips, checked against David Fowler's 2026 effort where AI agents opened about a hundred allocation PRs against ASP.NET Core: what still holds, what changed, and what the microbenchmarks did not show.
- [C++ stack corruption caused by an empty APIENTRY](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/cpp-stack-corruption-due-to-define/): How one empty #define APIENTRY made every OpenGL extension call on 32-bit Windows pop its arguments twice, why the x64 build never showed it, and how to make the bug impossible.
- [Property-based tests found two bugs our example tests never would](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/property-based-tests-found-two-bugs/): Adding fast-check to a React frontend: a saved cart where "abc" counted as 3 items, a translation key named valueOf that crashed the app, and a model test that runs 2000 cart sequences in a quarter of a second.
- [Replacing ESLint with Oxlint, custom rules included](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/eslint-to-oxlint-with-custom-rules/): Moving a React codebase from ESLint to Oxlint with its own lint rules: lint went from 17 s to 2 s, and here is what we lost, what broke quietly and what got slower.
- [Six months of agentic coding: what actually changed](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/six-months-of-agentic-coding-what-actually-changed/): After about 500 merged PRs with coding agents: write constraints instead of code, separate builder and critic, keep PRs small, and verify like a user.
- [Why std::expected matters for error handling](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/cpp-std-expected-and-std-error-code/): How C++23 std::expected and std::error_code work together: custom error categories, monadic chaining, and why an error category must be a single object per program.
- [Conan 2.x migration and the lessons learned](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/conan-2x-migration-lessons-learned/): Migrating a C++ product from Conan 1 to 2: recipe and package revisions, toolchain and deps generators, the Conan API, deployers and the pitfalls I hit.
- [Fix the ctypes _type_ error on Azure Pipelines](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/azure-pipelines-python-ctypes-importerror/): pip fails on a self-hosted Windows Azure Pipelines agent with "class must define a '_type_' attribute". Prepending Python's DLLs folder to PATH fixed it.
- [GitHub Actions: push to a repo with a deploy key](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/github-actions-deploy-with-permissions/): Fix the 403 when a GitHub Actions workflow pushes a Hugo build to another repository: use an SSH deploy key, clone the repo fresh and push HEAD:master.
- [Cross-platform Bash scripts in Azure Pipelines](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/azure-pipelines-cross-platform-scripts/): One Bash script for Windows, macOS and Linux Azure Pipelines agents: setting up Git for Windows bash and making a failing Bash step fail the job.
- [Running Python cross-platform in Azure Pipelines](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/azure-pipelines-cross-platform-python-scripting/): Make python vs python3 work on Windows, macOS and Linux self-hosted Azure Pipelines agents: UsePythonVersion limits, PATH and pip, in one template.
- [Typed Python CLI arguments with argparse and StrEnum](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/how-to-typed-command-line-arguments-in-python/): Derive argparse choices from Python types: use StrEnum and the type parameter so a build script's CLI options update when the enum changes.
- [Run a Python function by name from the command line](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/how-to-call-function-of-file-in-python/): Call any function in a Python script from the command line with positional or keyword arguments, using globals() and inspect.signature.
- [Practical C++17 highlights by example](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/practical-cppstd17/): Short C++17 examples: structured bindings, if constexpr, CTAD, std::variant, std::optional, string_view, filesystem and parallel algorithms.
- [std::variant: build an array of all alternatives](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/cpp-make-variant-alternatives-array/): Use variant_size and variant_alternative with an index sequence to build a compile-time array holding one instance of each std::variant alternative.
- [Build macOS Universal Binaries with Conan and CMake](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/how-to-build-macos-universal-binaries-with-conan-and-cmake/): Build x86_64 and arm64 macOS Universal Binaries with Conan and CMake: CMakeToolchain, Autotools, Boost, lipo and automated recipe patching.
- [How I finally finished my DIY smart mirror](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/how-a-smart-mirror-project-finished-after-years/): Building a smart mirror from scratch: wooden frame, spy-mirror film, a Vue.js dashboard, mounting, a bill of materials and what I'd do differently.
- [C# Performance - Profiling introduction](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/csharp-performance-profiling-introduction/): Profiling a C# WPF inspection app: hotspots, memory allocation, microarchitecture and threading efficiency with VTune, dotTrace and Visual Studio.
- [Reactive testing with Gherkin, ReactiveX and asyncio](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/reactive-testing-with-gherkin-reactivex-and-asyncio/): Replace time.sleep in async BDD integration tests: assert events with RxPy observables, pytest-bdd Gherkin steps and asyncio, on an MQTT example.
- [Secure Docker login credentials with pass on Linux](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/how-to-setup-docker-credential-store/): Stop Docker storing your password unencrypted: set up docker-credential-pass with pass and a GPG key on Ubuntu, plus the macOS and Windows helpers.
- [Set a Linux MAC address from EEPROM](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/how-to-set-linux-mac-address/): Read a MAC address from EEPROM with dd and hexdump, format it, and apply it to eth0 at runtime or permanently on an embedded Linux device.
- [An interactive Yocto shell for device provisioning](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/how-to-create-an-interactive-yocto-shell/): An interactive Yocto shell for factory provisioning: validated MAC input, flashing swupdate, erasing NOR flash and writing EEPROM on embedded Linux.
- [First Post](https://ovaar.github.io/blog/first-post/): Why I started a software engineering blog: writing about solutions I and colleagues built, reflecting on my career, and getting better at writing.
